chunks.heading: About our showcases
chunks.text:
Each term, our Knight Foundation School of Computing & Information Sciences (KFSCIS) seniors present their Capstone Projects — what we historically called Senior Projects. Summer showcases are hosted by KFSCIS on their own and held virtually. Fall showcases are typically coordinated with the broader College of Engineering & Computing (CEC) — sometimes co-located, sometimes spanning two days or multiple locations. Spring is the College's flagship Senior Design Showcase, bringing together students from every CEC school and department — across the College these projects are known as Senior Design Projects — typically on the last Friday of the semester, just before finals week, often at the FIU Arena. This site focuses on KFSCIS Capstone Projects; when an event is held jointly with the College, we'll note it, but our showcase pages center on our own students and their work.

chunks.heading: Showcase prep checklist
chunks.text:
Adapted for the virtual format from the College's event-preparation checklist.

Before

• Finalize and proofread your poster and slides; export to PDF.
• Record a backup demo video in case the live demo fails.
• Test your camera, mic, screen-share, and internet on the meeting platform.
• Rehearse a tight 3–5 minute pitch; time it; assign speaking parts.
• Prepare answers to likely judge questions about design and impact.

During

• Join early; confirm audio/video; close distracting apps and notifications.
• Share your screen deliberately; speak clearly; make eye contact with the camera.
• Lead with the problem and your solution; show the demo; invite questions.

After

• Share a project link (repo / demo) and your contact for follow-ups.
• Thank judges and sponsors; note their feedback while it's fresh.
• Keep your poster/slides — they're great portfolio and interview material.

The Capstone Program turns senior classes into engineering teams — guided by professional Scrum and AI-powered tooling.

Over Capstone I and Capstone II, students in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Data Science & AI form teams to take a project from concept to a working product — practicing requirements, architecture, agile delivery, and professional presentation. Projects culminate in our end-of-term showcases — hosted virtually by KFSCIS in the summer, and as part of the College of Engineering & Computing Senior Design Showcase in the spring — where teams demo their work to faculty, industry judges, and the public.

In the College's own words, the capstone is a junior course (Capstone 1) and a senior course (Capstone 2), run in an Agile environment, in faculty-supervised teams of up to five members. Capstone 1 lays the groundwork — requirements, design, and planning — and Capstone 2 delivers and presents the working product.

A note on terminology: at KFSCIS we call these Capstone Projects (formerly "Senior Projects"); across the wider College of Engineering & Computing the same work is known as Senior Design Projects. (College program description)

This site publishes project titles, disciplines, and abstracts so the community can explore what FIU computing students build each term. Participants (students, reviewers, and faculty) sign in for the live portal.

chunks.heading: Our Capstone Story
chunks.text:
Prof. S. Masoud Sadjadi has been an FIU professor since Fall 2004. He took over the Senior Project course and ran the first showcase in Fall 2012 — and the showcase has run every semester since Fall 2012, never interrupted: three per year (Fall, Spring, and Summer), with summers held virtually, and continuing virtually through COVID.

Long known as “Senior Projects,” the program is today the FIU KFSCIS Capstone — across the College of Engineering & Computing the same work is known as Senior Design Projects.

chunks.heading: Frequently asked
chunks.text:
Does engaging cost money?

No — mentoring, judging, and hiring are free; only sponsorship involves funds, and even that has a no-cost "gift" structure.

Who owns the intellectual property?

By default, the students who build it. With IP-protected sponsorship, your company — via a student-to-company assignment plus a standard FIU educational carve-out.

How much time is it?

Mentor/PO ≈ 1–2 hrs per 2-week sprint; judging ≈ 2–3 hours.

Can I hire the students?

Yes — many partners recruit interns and new grads after seeing them work.

What about confidentiality / NDAs?

Available on the IP-protected lane; students are always offered a non-proprietary alternative with no grade impact, and FIU retains a copy for accreditation under confidentiality.

How do I start?

The short form below — tell us how you'd like to engage and we'll follow up.

chunks.heading: Primary Logo Guidelines

The FIU logo is essential to our visual brand and website. It represents the entire university. Our logo is likely the first thing our audience sees and might be the last thing they remember. There are several versions of the FIU logo for different use cases. Most colleges and large units around the university have an FIU logo unique to them.

The Primary FIU Logo is the most used and recognizable version of our brand. There are three versions of the primary logo, and selecting the right one depends on format, available space, audience and readability.

• Use any version of the primary logos for all internal university-wide communications, marketing initiatives and web ads. Prioritize using the horizontal or vertical versions of the logo unless space is limited.
• Use either the horizontal or vertical versions of the logo for official university documents.
• Use either the horizontal or vertical versions of the logo for non-local audiences, national or international web ads and marketing initiatives.
• The primary acronym logo should only be used for marketing materials, never for official university documents.
• The primary acronym logo may be used on its own for on-campus marketing materials and events.
• Do not combine the primary acronym logo with an official unit logo.

• Use either the horizontal or vertical versions of the logo for non-local audiences, national or international web ads and marketing initiatives.
• The primary acronym logo should only be used for marketing materials, never for official university documents.
• The primary acronym logo may be used on its own for on-campus marketing materials and events.
• Do not combine the primary acronym logo with an official unit logo.

chunks.heading: Brand Colors
chunks.text:
Colors play a pivotal role in establishing FIU’s identity and conveying our values and character to the world. Using official university colors and their variations is essential for maintaining brand consistency and recognition. These colors have been carefully chosen to reflect the institution’s heritage, values and mission.

Adhering to these specific colors and avoiding those of competing brands ensures our visual identity remains distinctive and memorable. Our colors are not just a matter of aesthetics but a powerful tool for reinforcing our brand and leaving a lasting impression on students, alumni and the wider community.

chunks.heading: Ways to engage with FIU Capstone
chunks.text: Substance, not label — what changes hands decides the lane
blocks: Substance, not label — what changes hands decides the lane

chunks.heading: Ways to engage — the lanes, explained
hierarchy: Ways to engage — the lanes, explained
chunks.text:
You are not locked into one choice. You can hold more than one engagement at the same time, and move between lanes as your goals change. We revisit the fit together at the start of each term.

Lane | Funding | Who owns IP | NDA | FIU office
A · Open | none | students | no | none
B · Gift | gift | students | no | FIU Foundation (managed through the University's Foundation-to-ORED gift process)
C · Deliverables | fee | students (+ license) | no | Pre-Award
D · Proprietary | fee | you | yes | ORED / OGC
E · Research | contract | per contract | per contract | ORED
Time & talent | none | n/a | no | none

Always — two protections on every paid lane (C / D / E)

• Educational / accreditation carve-out — FIU keeps a copy of the work for teaching, assessment, and ABET review, shown to evaluators under confidentiality. Nothing is made public without your agreement; a sanitized showcase poster is always allowed.
• Student-choice protection — no student is forced to assign IP or sign an NDA; a non-proprietary alternative always exists; and a student's grade is never affected by these choices.

If your organization also posts roles through Capstone Careers: giving confers no advantage in the marketplace. Roles rank on engagement — projects sponsored, showcases judged, students mentored and hired — never on what you give.

Become a sponsor

This is the same explanation you'll see in the onboarding wizard when you add a project — one source of truth. — Masoud Sadjadi

chunks.heading: About our showcases
chunks.text:
Each term, our Knight Foundation School of Computing & Information Sciences (KFSCIS) seniors present their Capstone Projects — what we historically called Senior Projects. Summer showcases are hosted by KFSCIS on their own and held virtually. Fall showcases are typically coordinated with the broader College of Engineering & Computing (CEC) — sometimes co-located, sometimes spanning two days or multiple locations. Spring is the College's flagship Senior Design Showcase, bringing together students from every CEC school and department — across the College these projects are known as Senior Design Projects — typically on the last Friday of the semester, just before finals week, often at the FIU Arena. This site focuses on KFSCIS Capstone Projects; when an event is held jointly with the College, we'll note it, but our showcase pages center on our own students and their work.

chunks.heading: About our showcases
chunks.text:
Each term, our Knight Foundation School of Computing & Information Sciences (KFSCIS) seniors present their Capstone Projects — what we historically called Senior Projects. Summer showcases are hosted by KFSCIS on their own and held virtually. Fall showcases are typically coordinated with the broader College of Engineering & Computing (CEC) — sometimes co-located, sometimes spanning two days or multiple locations. Spring is the College's flagship Senior Design Showcase, bringing together students from every CEC school and department — across the College these projects are known as Senior Design Projects — typically on the last Friday of the semester, just before finals week, often at the FIU Arena. This site focuses on KFSCIS Capstone Projects; when an event is held jointly with the College, we'll note it, but our showcase pages center on our own students and their work.

chunks.heading: About our showcases
chunks.text:
Each term, our Knight Foundation School of Computing & Information Sciences (KFSCIS) seniors present their Capstone Projects — what we historically called Senior Projects. Summer showcases are hosted by KFSCIS on their own and held virtually. Fall showcases are typically coordinated with the broader College of Engineering & Computing (CEC) — sometimes co-located, sometimes spanning two days or multiple locations. Spring is the College's flagship Senior Design Showcase, bringing together students from every CEC school and department — across the College these projects are known as Senior Design Projects — typically on the last Friday of the semester, just before finals week, often at the FIU Arena. This site focuses on KFSCIS Capstone Projects; when an event is held jointly with the College, we'll note it, but our showcase pages center on our own students and their work.

chunks.heading: About our showcases
chunks.text:
Each term, our Knight Foundation School of Computing & Information Sciences (KFSCIS) seniors present their Capstone Projects — what we historically called Senior Projects. Summer showcases are hosted by KFSCIS on their own and held virtually. Fall showcases are typically coordinated with the broader College of Engineering & Computing (CEC) — sometimes co-located, sometimes spanning two days or multiple locations. Spring is the College's flagship Senior Design Showcase, bringing together students from every CEC school and department — across the College these projects are known as Senior Design Projects — typically on the last Friday of the semester, just before finals week, often at the FIU Arena. This site focuses on KFSCIS Capstone Projects; when an event is held jointly with the College, we'll note it, but our showcase pages center on our own students and their work.

Two of those pavilions are where our computing projects fit: Enterprise IT & Cybersecurity and AI & Machine Learning. For that joint event's logistics, registration, sponsorship, and judging, see capstone.cec.fiu.edu. Our Summer KFSCIS Virtual Showcase above remains our own primary event.

chunks.heading: About our showcases
chunks.text:
Each term, our Knight Foundation School of Computing & Information Sciences (KFSCIS) seniors present their Capstone Projects — what we historically called Senior Projects. Summer showcases are hosted by KFSCIS on their own and held virtually. Fall showcases are typically coordinated with the broader College of Engineering & Computing (CEC) — sometimes co-located, sometimes spanning two days or multiple locations. Spring is the College's flagship Senior Design Showcase, bringing together students from every CEC school and department — across the College these projects are known as Senior Design Projects — typically on the last Friday of the semester, just before finals week, often at the FIU Arena. This site focuses on KFSCIS Capstone Projects; when an event is held jointly with the College, we'll note it, but our showcase pages center on our own students and their work.

chunks.heading: About our showcases
chunks.text:
Each term, our Knight Foundation School of Computing & Information Sciences (KFSCIS) seniors present their Capstone Projects — what we historically called Senior Projects. Summer showcases are hosted by KFSCIS on their own and held virtually. Fall showcases are typically coordinated with the broader College of Engineering & Computing (CEC) — sometimes co-located, sometimes spanning two days or multiple locations. Spring is the College's flagship Senior Design Showcase, bringing together students from every CEC school and department — across the College these projects are known as Senior Design Projects — typically on the last Friday of the semester, just before finals week, often at the FIU Arena. This site focuses on KFSCIS Capstone Projects; when an event is held jointly with the College, we'll note it, but our showcase pages center on our own students and their work.
